subject: Digital Electronics
course: Edge AI and Embedded Machine Learning
learning_objective: Convert real values into signed int8 codes and reconstruct them, separating rounding error from saturation.
core_conclusion: Int8 stores an integer code; scale and zero point recover an approximation, while out-of-range values saturate.

terminology.scope: Official terminology basis from saved course research; all numerical examples are explicitly illustrative.

scenes.heading: A real value meets an integer grid
scenes.change: Float markers appear between representable positions; the selected marker exposes x/scale+z = −1.6.
scenes.cause: An affine encoding maps real units to code units.
scenes.result: The selected float sits between the integer codes −2 and −1.
scenes.timing_reason: 4 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Round to the nearest code
scenes.change: Markers snap to reconstructed positions −0.3,0.1,0.9 as their codes become −6,−2,6.

scenes.timing_reason: 5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Recover an approximation
lines: A smaller representation can lose detail.
scenes.change: The −2 code subtracts −3 and multiplies by 0.1; the output marker lands at 0.1 while the original stays at 0.14.
scenes.cause: Dequantization applies the inverse affine map to the rounded code.
scenes.result: An error bracket measures 0.04, making the loss visible.
scenes.timing_reason: 5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Outside the range, values clip
lines: Clipping is larger than rounding error.
scenes.change: An input14 attempts code137; it reaches the code boundary127 and reconstructs to13 instead of14.
scenes.cause: Signed int8 cannot represent a code above127.
scenes.result: The endpoint and the lost one-unit segment remain visible.
scenes.timing_reason: 5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

final_title: Quantization from Float32 to Int8: Rounding and Clipping
title: Quantization from Float32 to Int8: Rounding and Clipping
prompt:
Create a 30-second silent English animation of Quantization from Float32 to Int8. At 0–6 s, place −0.26, 0.14 and 0.87 on a real-value grid with scale 0.1 and zero point −3. At 6–14 s, snap them to int8 codes −6, −2 and 6 and reconstructed values −0.3, 0.1 and 0.9. At 14–22 s, reconstruct code −2 and expose its 0.04 error. At 22–30 s, show input 14 attempting code 137, saturating at 127 and reconstructing to 13.

Render a 1920×1080, 16:9 MP4 at 30 fps with no audio, using Helvetica Neue and line height 1.45. Use background layers #0e0e0e, #171b1c and #212629; input #56b4e9, operations #e69f00, results #009e73, clipping or rejection #d55e00, and secondary weights #cc79a7, with strong text #f8fafc and muted text #a8b4c4. Keep concise copy left and a large numerical SVG diagram right; fade and slide labels over 12–18 frames with 10-frame staggering, and bind moving marks, values and arithmetic to the same mechanism state.
